I've been farming this land since I was 14. Peanuts are what I know. My 4.1 mu is not much, but it feeds my wife and me and gives us some income. I don't overthink this — I've seen what works here in Quzhou over 56 years.

**Seed:** I'll buy improved seed from the township supply cooperative again. They've been selling these better varieties for twenty years now. My neighbor uses them too. They sprout more evenly than the old seeds I saved myself.

**Fertilizer:** Before planting I'll apply compound fertilizer as base — I've always done this. Peanuts pull their own nitrogen from the soil, so I don't put down much urea. Phosphorus matters for the pods, so I give it more of that. I'll mix in some potash too. Same as last year.

**Irrigation:** My well is reliable. I water before planting to get moisture right, then again at flowering, then once more when pods are filling. Three times is enough. More than that wastes money and my back can't handle more pumping.

**Tillage:** I'll hire the rotary tiller from the village machinery station. I can't plough myself anymore at my age, and rotary is fine for peanuts — breaks up the soil well enough.

**Pesticides:** I'll spray once early for seed protection and soil insects, and once in summer for leaf spot. Two times is what I've always done.

**Yield:** In a normal year, I get around 290 jin per mu of fresh pods — call it 290 kg. Weather permitting.
